WHOLE — SPECIFICATION

BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002

Price Group 1 



Spices and Condiments Sectional Committee, FAD 9 



FOREWORD 



This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the 
draft finalized by the Spices and Condiments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food 
and Agriculture Division Council. 

Fennel seeds, commonly known as SAUNF, are one of the spices exported from India. A sizable 
quantity of these seeds is exported to United Kingdom and to some of the European and Middle 
Eastern countries. They are also known to be extensively used within the country for culinary 
purposes and for preparing indigenous medicines, essences, etc. 

This standard was first issued in 1966. This revision is brought out for incorporating the latest 
developments m the field and also to align to International Standard. Requirements for extraneous 
matter have been incorporated and the requirements for moisture reviewed and updated. 

This standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration 
Act, 1954 and the Rules framed thereunder, wherever applicable. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded offm accordance with IS 2 : 1960 < Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised) 9 . 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded of! value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard 

SPICES AND CONDIMENTS - FENNEL 
WHOLE— SPECIFICATION 

(First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

This standard prescribes the requirements for 
dried fruits ( seeds ) of fennel ( Foeniculum 
vulgare Mill,). 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

ISNo. Title 

1070:1992 Reagent grade water ( third 

revision ) 

1797 : 1985 Methods of test for spices and 

condiments ( second revision ) 

13145 : 1993 Spices and condiments — 

Methods of sampling {first 
revision ) 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the 
following definitions shall apply. 

3.1,1 Extraneous Matter 

It includes organic matter, such as calyx pieces, 
stalklets, loose tops, stem, straw or any other 
vegetable matter. It also includes inorganic 
matter such as dust, dirt, stones, lumps of 
earth, sand and grit. 



3.1.2 Damaged^ Discoloured and Weeviled Seeds 

This includes fennel seeds that are damaged or 
discolured so as to affect the quality of the 
material and also includes seeds showing signs 
of bores in the seeds as a result of their having 
been eaten up by weevils or insects. 

3.1.3 Shrivelled and Immature Seeds 



These are seeds 
developed. 

4 GRADES 



that have not been properly 



4.1 Fennel seeds shall be of three grades, 
namely, special, good and fair ( see Table 1 ). 

5 REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Description 

The fennel seeds shall be the dried fruits 
( seeds ) of Foeniculum vulgare Mill. Seeds shall 
be yellowish green to drak green in colour, and 
shall have the characteristic size and shape of 
type or variety. The seeds shall be reasonably 
dry. 

5.2 Taste and Flavour 

The taste and flavour of fennel seeds shall be 
fresh and characteristic of the type and variety. 
The material shall be free from foreign taste 
and flavour as well as from any musty odour.

5.3 Freedom from Moulds and Insects 

Fennel seeds shall be free from visible insect 
and moulds, and shall be practically free from 
dead insects and contamination by rodents, 
visible to the naked eye, corrected, if necessary, 
in any particular case. In case the magnifica- 
tion exceeds X 10, this fact should be stated in 
the test report. 

5.4 The grade designation and the requirements 
for each of them shall be as given in Table 1. 

6 PACKING 

Fennel seeds shall be packed in sound, clean 
and dry containers made of jute, cloth, paper 
or polyethylene. The containers shall be free 
from insect or fungal infestation as well as from 
any undesirable odour. 

7 MARKING 

7.1 The following particulars shall be marked 
or labelled on each container: 



a) Name of the 
designation; 



material and grade 



b) Variety of trade name or brand name, if 
any; 

c) Batch or code number; 

d) Net mass 

e) Date of packing; and 

f) Country of origin. 

8 SAMPLING 

8.1 Representative samples of fennel seeds 
shall be drawn according to IS 13145 : 1993. 

9 TESTS 

9.1 Tests shall be carried out in accordance 
with Table 1. 

9.2 Quality of Reagents 

Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and 
distilled water ( see IS 1070 : 1992 ) shall be 
employed in tests 

NOTE — 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that 
do not contain impurities' which affect the results of 
analysis.
